bear.text: The company disclosed on 2 September 2026 that it received a GST demand order for ₹46.3 crore, including interest and penalty, related to input tax credits claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22.
The CFO stated that receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year, attributing the rise mainly to slower payments from two large state utility customers.
EBITDA margin contracted by 170 basis points to 11.2% in Q1 FY27, which the Managing Director said was affected by a sharp rise in copper prices during the quarter.

bull.text: The order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year ago.
Management said the new Bharuch plant, adding about 30% to cable capacity, is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27 and will contribute from the second half.
The Managing Director said data-centre cables are now about 9 percent of domestic revenue and thinks that can double in two years.
Institutional ownership increased, with foreign institutional investors holding 11.8% and domestic institutional investors holding 14.6% as of June 2026, up from 9.2% and 12.7% a year earlier.

open_questions.text: The company's press release reports Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹1,248 crore, while a news article reports it as ₹1,428 crore. What explains this discrepancy in the reported revenue figure?

The company says it intends to file an appeal against the ₹46.3 crore GST demand and does not expect a material impact on its financial position. What is the timeline for this appeal and what are the potential financial implications if the appeal is unsuccessful?

The Managing Director stated that about two-thirds of contracts have price-variation clauses that reset with a lag of one to two quarters. How quickly can the company pass on the current rise in copper costs to customers to restore margins?

snapshot.text: Sarvottam Cables Ltd is a manufacturer of power cables, wires and conductors.
For the quarter ended 30 June 2026, the company reported revenue from operations of ₹1,248 crore and profit after tax of ₹82 crore.
EBITDA for Q1 FY27 was ₹140 crore, resulting in an EBITDA margin of 11.2%.
Promoters and the promoter group held 58.2% of the company's shares as of June 2026.
